**Recommendation for Covering GLP‑1 Medications (Semaglutide (“Wegovy”), Tirzepatide) for Obesity in a 5,000‑Employee Self‑Insured Plan** | Domain | Key Take‑aways | Practical Actions | |--------|----------------|-------------------| | **Clinical** | • Semaglutide is FDA‑approved for obesity; tirzepatide has Phase III data (SURMOUNT‑1) but is off‑label.
• Both agents improve weight, glycaemic control, and cardiovascular risk factors.
• Safety profile: GI intolerance, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease; no confirmed human MTC signal. | • Cover semaglutide for obesity per AACE/ADA guidelines (BMI ≥35 kg/m² or ≥30 kg/m² + comorbidity).
• Consider a pilot for tirzepatide with strict medical‑necessity documentation and outcome‑based rebates. | | **Legal** | • ERISA requires coverage to be “reasonable and necessary.”
• ADA/EEOC prohibit denial solely on BMI; coverage may still be denied if not medically necessary.
• Off‑label use is permissible under ERISA with appropriate justification. | • Embed a medical‑necessity clause referencing AACE/ADA guidelines in the plan documents and PBM contracts.
• Require prior‑authorization (PA) that records BMI, comorbidities, lifestyle attempts, baseline labs, and off‑label justification for tirzepatide. | | **Financial** | • List price ≈ $1,200/month for Wegovy; net cost after rebates ≈ $720–$960/month.
• If 5 % of members (≈250) use the drug: gross $300k/month → $60 PMPM; with a Tier‑2 copay ($30) → ~$30 PMPM net.
• Potential savings from reduced diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia are **model‑based** (~$150–$250/member over 3 yrs); real‑world data will refine this estimate. | • Conduct a 3‑year budget‑impact analysis using actual enrollment, adherence, and net cost data.
• Negotiate outcome‑based rebates (e.g., $200 rebate per member who loses ≥5 % body weight at 6 months).
• Place GLP‑1 agents in Tier 2; consider a higher copay for tirzepatide pending contract terms. | --- ## 1. Executive Summary Covering semaglutide (FDA‑approved) and, on a pilot basis, tirzepatide (off‑label) can improve employee health outcomes while aligning with preventive care goals. A policy that balances evidence‑based clinical criteria, ERISA/ADA compliance, and prudent financial stewardship will allow the employer to offer these medications responsibly. --- ## 2. Clinical Considerations | Element | Recommendation | |---------|----------------| | **Indication** | • Semaglutide (Wegovy) – FDA‑approved for obesity.
• Tirzepatide – Phase III SURMOUNT‑1 data show mean weight loss ≈ 15 % at 68 weeks; not yet FDA‑approved for obesity but may be covered off‑label with robust documentation. | | **Eligibility Criteria** | • BMI ≥ 35 kg/m², or <35 kg/m² if ≥30 kg/m² + at least one obesity‑related comorbidity (HTN, dyslipidaemia, OSA, pre‑diabetes).
• Document ≥3 months of supervised lifestyle therapy failure (dietitian counselling + structured exercise). | | **Baseline & Monitoring Labs** | • CBC, CMP, lipid panel, HbA1c, TSH.
• Repeat at 6 months; additional labs only if clinically indicated. | | **Safety Profile** | • Common adverse events: nausea/vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain (pancreatitis).
• Gallbladder disease reported in clinical trials.
• No confirmed increased risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) in humans; exclude patients with MEN‑2 or personal/family history of thyroid cancer. | | **Duration & Re‑evaluation** | • Allow continuous therapy up to 24 months per episode, with quarterly review for benefit and safety.
• Extension beyond 24 months is permissible if ongoing clinical benefit is documented. | --- ## 3. Legal Considerations 1. **ERISA – “Reasonable and Necessary”** - Coverage decisions must be defensible under ERISA; use AACE/ADA guidelines as a standard of care. 2. **Anti‑Discrimination (ADA, EEOC)** - Denial solely on BMI is prohibited. Coverage may still be denied if the treatment is not medically necessary per accepted clinical standards. 3. **FDA Approval Status** - Semaglutide: covered under FDA labeling for obesity. - Tirzepatide: off‑label; coverage requires documented medical necessity and a clear justification that no other approved therapy is appropriate. 4. **Documentation & Liability** - Maintain detailed PA records (BMI, comorbidities, lifestyle attempts, baseline labs). - Implement adverse event reporting to monitor safety and mitigate liability. 5. **PBM Contractual Language** - Include explicit clauses that the PA workflow and medical‑necessity criteria are binding; specify penalties for arbitrary denial. --- ## 4. Financial Considerations | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | **Net Cost Estimates** | • Semaglutide: list $1,200/month → net $720–$960/month after typical rebates (20–40 %).
• Tirzepatide: list $1,400/month → net $840–$1,120/month. | | **PMPM Cost Projection** | • 5 % of 5,000 employees ≈ 250 members use the drug.
• Gross cost = 250 × $1,200 = $300,000/month → $60 PMPM.
• With Tier‑2 copay ($30), net PMPM ≈ $30. | | **Budget Impact (3‑Year Model)** | • Incremental annual cost: ~$3.6 M (gross) → ~$1.8–$2.4 M after rebates.
• Potential offset from reduced diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia: $150–$250/member over 3 yrs → ~$750k–$1.25 M savings. | | **Risk‑Sharing / Outcome Rebates** | • Negotiate manufacturer rebates tied to ≥5 % weight loss at 6 months (e.g., $200 rebate per qualifying member).
• Such contracts are emerging but can be complex; involve clear performance metrics and audit rights. | | **Tier Placement** | • Semaglutide: Tier‑2 copay $30/month.
• Tirzepatide: consider higher copay or separate tier pending outcome contract terms. | --- ## 5. Utilization Management Strategy 1. **Prior Authorization (PA)** - Mandatory for all GLP‑1 prescriptions.
- PA form auto‑populates BMI, comorbidities, lifestyle attempts, baseline labs, and off‑label justification (for tirzepatide).
- Approval within 48 hrs; denial requires documentation of medical necessity failure. 2. **Step Therapy** - First line: intensive lifestyle program (dietitian + structured exercise) for ≥6 months.
- Second line: GLP‑1 if step 1 fails (≤5 % weight loss at 6 months). 3. **Quantity Limits & Duration** - Initial fill limited to 12 weeks; re‑authorization required after 24 weeks unless clinically justified.
- Total annual quantity capped at 48 weeks per member. 4. **Monitoring Schedule** - Weight check every 12 weeks (via pharmacy or primary care).
- Labs: baseline, 6 months, then annually if continued therapy.
- Adverse event reporting mandatory for pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, severe GI intolerance. 5. **Discontinuation Criteria** - Persistent GI intolerance, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, or lack of ≥3 % weight loss at 6 months → discontinue and document reason. --- ## 6. Implementation Plan | Phase | Actions | |-------|---------| | **Stakeholder Engagement** | • Medical director, pharmacy benefit manager (PBM), legal counsel, finance team, HR, employee representatives. | | **Pilot Program** | • Enroll 200–300 members with BMI ≥35 kg/m²; include a matched control group (lifestyle only) for comparative analysis. | | **Data Collection & Reporting** | • Use integrated EMR/claims dashboard to track utilization, cost, weight loss outcomes, and adverse events.
- Quarterly reports to medical director and finance. | | **Policy Finalization** | • Refine PA workflow, tier placement, and outcome‑rebate terms based on pilot data. | | **Communication** | • Roll out via intranet, webinars, FAQ sheets; emphasize eligibility, benefits, and cost‑sharing structure. | | **Ongoing Review** | • Quarterly review of utilization patterns; adjust PA criteria or tier copays as needed.
- Annual audit of legal compliance and financial impact. | --- ## 7. Recommendation Summary 1. **Cover semaglutide (Wegovy) for obesity** under a Tier‑2 copay with mandatory prior authorization, BMI ≥35 kg/m² (or ≥30 kg/m² + comorbidity), and documented lifestyle failure. 2. **Pilot tirzepatide on an off‑label basis**, requiring stricter medical‑necessity documentation and outcome‑based rebates; consider a higher copay pending contract terms. 3. **Implement a robust utilization‑management framework**: step therapy, PA workflow, quantity limits, monitoring schedule, and clear discontinuation criteria. 4. **Negotiate risk‑sharing contracts** that tie manufacturer rebates to clinically meaningful weight loss (≥5 % at 6 months). 5. **Ensure legal compliance** by embedding medical‑necessity language in plan documents and PBM contracts, documenting all PA decisions, and protecting against ADA/EEOC discrimination claims. 6. **Monitor financial impact** through a 3‑year budget‑impact model; adjust tier placement or utilization limits based on real‑world data. By adopting this balanced approach, the employer can provide evidence‑based obesity treatment, safeguard employee health, manage costs prudently, and demonstrate leadership in preventive care.
